title: Grace only perfects and helps nature
source_text: XCIX. Jam autem Doctor ille non aliud gratiae tribuit quam ut perficiat naturam, eamque adjuvet in suis motibus, ut unusquisque ex supernaturali auxilio & gratia talis sit, qualis ad salutem oportet. Ac proinde ad dignoscendos & explicandos motus gratiae, vult attendi ad progressum & ordinem, quem natura ipsa, potentiaeve cognoscentes & appetentes servarent, si illos eosdem actus, qui gratiae tribuuntur, suis solis viribus quoad substantiam actus producerent, quod fieri posse ille existimat. Ut ea ratione intelligatur quo pacto Deus per auxilia ac dona gratiae, se inserat & cooperetur cum natura, eamque adjuvet, ut supra suas vires eos actus producat quales ad salutem necessarii sunt.
pass_a_gloss: XCIX. Now that Doctor attributes nothing else to grace than that it perfect nature, and help it in its motions, so that each one from supernatural aid & grace be such, as is needful for salvation. And therefore for discerning & explaining the motions of grace, he wants attention paid to the progress & order, which nature itself, or the knowing & appetitive powers would keep, if they produced those same acts, which are attributed to grace, by their own forces alone as to the substance of the act, which he thinks can be done. That in that way it may be understood how God through the aids and gifts of grace, inserts himself & cooperates with nature, and helps it, that above its forces it produce those acts such as are necessary for salvation.
pass_b_english: Thesis XCIX. Molina gives grace no other role than to perfect nature and help it in its own motions, so that each person becomes, through supernatural aid and grace, what salvation requires. To identify and explain the motions of grace, therefore, he wants us to look at the course and order that nature itself, or the knowing and desiring powers, would follow if they produced, by their own strength alone, the substance of the same acts that are attributed to grace. He thinks this can happen.

In this way we are to understand how God, through the aids and gifts of grace, inserts himself into nature, cooperates with it and helps it, so that it produces beyond its own strength such acts as are necessary for salvation.
